title: Bundle sampler latency probe and kernel parameterization for embedding endpoint tail reduction
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Objective: Reduce p95/p99 latency for the embeddings endpoint under bursty ingress by introducing a bundle-sampler micro-batching policy and tuning low-level kernel parameters. Background: Recent telemetry shows sporadic tail spikes correlated with request-size heterogeneity and occasional kernel inefficiencies when sequence lengths vary. Existing microbatcher aggregates by arrival time; we believe grouping by a lightweight bundle-sampler heuristic (sequence length + tenant fingerprint) will improve packing density and reduce stalls without raising median latency significantly. Proposal: 1) Implement an experimental bundle-sampler microbatch policy in the short-lived batching layer (can be toggled per endpoint). 2) Run a parameter sweep for kernel-level knobs (prefetch depth, compute tile size, thread-affinity) on a dedicated staging shard. 3) Add end-to-end tracing tags for bundle_id, chosen_kernel_profile, and KV-cache hit/warm metrics. 4) Canary rollout with traffic shadowing and a ramped A/B where 10% of traffic uses the bundle sampler and tuned kernels. Success metrics: reduce embedding endpoint p99 by >=20% in production-like workloads; no increase in error rate or OOM frequency. Risks and mitigation: - Over-aggressive packing could increase transient memory use -> add per-bundle size cap. - Kernel changes might regress some model variants -> fallback to baseline kernels on degraded QPS or observed output regression. - Many tenants could be sensitive to latency variance -> honor tenant priority stack and exclude enterprise SLAs from experimental routing.
